There are usually not many skilled professionals available in the communities we select to work in. Those available usually cannot afford to travel to far off places in search of work. We therefore intend to provide educational and training facilities for these skilled professionals so that they develop their skills further. This will be in form of vocational skills, construction, teaching skills, art and crafts, photography and events organizing, all in line with their interests.

Community resource centers
The construction of the community centers in the slums we work in will be aimed at not only providing shelter to the families but will also be aimed at sensitizing the community about the importance of clean environments and hygiene. These community centers will be built with materials that are locally available and affordable. We shall therefore be focusing on materials such as earth blocks, bamboo sticks, metal, thatching grass, wood and rocks. The roofs of the centers will be water proof to ensure that the homes remain dry even during heavy rains.

The homes will also be spacious and have several rooms so as to provide a number of activities and services to the community that are currently unavailable. We shall also be providing training and tools so that the community can develop some skills to construct their own homes and those of their neighbors. This will in the long run ensure that the community can provide for themselves and empower themselves as they become more independent.

Environmental conservation.
The communities we work in usually do not have any environmental facilities such as parks. As a result, they usually dump their garbage indiscriminately or burn it. This has been detrimental to their health because most of the children have asthma and other diseases. By creating parks, they will have a place to dispose of their garbage. The parks will also provide play grounds for the children in the community and will therefore reduce the cases of diseases such as asthma that are caused by indoor conditions. We shall also provide the necessary tools and skills so that the community can maintain and develop the parks on their own.

Water for survival
The provision of water is very important to the community we work in because more than 80% of the people rely on contaminated water for their survival. The water provided in the community is usually contaminated and leads to water borne diseases. Providing clean and safe water will therefore be a great achievement because it will reduce the cases of diseases. The water will be channeled to the community center where it will be distributed to the community. We will also provide training and tools to help the community ensure that the water is safe for use. We will provide clean water through boreholes in the communities, water pans and irrigation farming.

Youth participation
The participation of the youth in the development activities will be another major achievement because most of them are idle and unemployed. They usually end up engaging in negative activities such as drug abuse and crime. This usually further worsens the situation in the community because some of them end up in jail. The youth will be involved in providing the resources such as labor and skills. They will also be involved in the construction of the centers, which will give them an opportunity to earn an income and develop their skills.

Old Cockie, who fathered a line of more manageable sheep dogs with the requisite willingness to work sheep. It was Old Cockie’s grandson, Wiston Cap, whose progeny founded the modern border collie breed in the 1900s. The modern border collie continues to be revered for its versatility, intelligence, and eagerness to please, and is the most popular working sheepdog in the world.

Living Conditions

Border collies are a herding dog at heart and enjoy being challenged. As such, they are happiest in a home where they have plenty of room to roam, with a fenced yard or access to a large field being preferable to an apartment. Border collies are more inclined to roam than many other breeds, and are known for their ability to jump tall fences, so they require a secure yard and close supervision. Border collies also have a long, coarse coat that makes them unsuitable for indoors, as their fur tends to shed profusely. They’re also prone to excessive barking, which can upset the neighbors. This makes them unsuitable for apartment-dwelling.

Border collies are also prone to separation anxiety, and they need a lot of attention and stimulation to keep them happy. They’re not suitable for a family that will be away from the house for a long period.

The Consensus Curriculum is integrated into the specific process to strive toward a deeper understanding and proficiency of the concepts. The curriculum follows and advances the mission and vision of the Diocese of Richmond regarding faith-based education.

The mission of the Consensus Curriculum is to provide students with a consistent curriculum, with rigorous standards, relative to their age and developmental stage. This will result in the students receiving a homogeneous curriculum that will support their advancement to the next intellectual level and beyond. Furthermore, the students will be prepared to compete successfully in college, the workforce, and in society, as a whole. The curriculum will also foster intellectual, critical thinking skills, while promoting personal, social, spiritual development.


The Consensus Curriculum is designed to support critical thinking skills and cognitive development through the following methods:

  1. Learning occurs through the development of critical thinking skills: applying information to a situation, analyzing information, categorizing information, comparing and contrasting information, drawing conclusions based on information, evaluating information, identifying information, inferring information, interpreting information, predicting information, reading information, recalling information, summarizing information, synthesizing information, and using information.
  2. Learning occurs through the development of analysis skills: determine the elements of a concept, determine the purpose of a concept, recognize the process of a concept, recognize the results of a concept, apply analysis skills to a problem, apply analysis skills to evaluate information, and identify the analysis skills utilized to analyze a concept.
  3. Learning occurs through the development of deductive and inductive reasoning skills: evaluate information, recognize similarities and differences in information, recognize the parts of information, recognize the qualities of information, and identify logic.
  4. Learning occurs through the development of clarity of thought skills: organize information, use appropriate vocabulary, correct grammatical usage, and support a position with evidence.
  5. Learning occurs through the development of problem solving skills: consider multiple strategies, evaluate the effectiveness of strategies, identify a problem, identify the goal, sequence the steps to solve the problem, utilize the problem-solving process, recognize when the problem is solved, and identify when a new problem develops.
  6. Learning occurs through the development of effective strategies: analyze a problem, collect information, generate alternatives, identify multiple solutions, formulate a plan, implement the plan, assess the effectiveness of the plan, recognize when the problem is solved, and identify a new problem.

The Consensus Curriculum will lead students to develop a deep understanding of the subject matter and provide them with the ability to successfully apply their knowledge to problem solving. The concepts and goals are accomplished through concept development, which supports the development of critical thinking skills. The students will be supported through the use of discussion, debate, inquiry, analysis, deductive and inductive reasoning, clarity of thought, problem solving, effective strategies, and assessment. The teachers will provide support and modeling of these skills and critical thinking through discussion, demonstration, inquiry, questioning, debate, and problem solving. The students will be given opportunities to practice these skills in and out of the classroom. In addition, students will be given opportunities to apply what they have learned to real-life situations.

Leith Links. Leith Links is situated in the north side of Edinburgh next to the Firth of Forth. It is located in the parish of Leith. The links was originally used by residents of the town of Leith. However, the links later became a popular spot for golfers, and it became an integral part of the history of golf. Golf was introduced to Scotland in the 1400's, with the first reference to the game being made in 1457. It was played by all classes of society, from peasants to the Royal family, and in 1459 the Scottish Parliament outlawed the game, as it was seen to be interfering with archery practice. However, the game proved to be too popular, and it was decided that golf could be played on the links of Leith. It was here that the game was transformed from a pastime to a sport. The Leith Links was used by golfers for more than 400 years, and it still boasts some of the finest fairways and greens in Scotland. The links at Leith are also famous for the Leith Links Golf Club, which was founded in 1818. The club has a long and illustrious history, with many famous golfers and captains having been members. In 2004, the club celebrated its 200th anniversary with a special tournament. The Leith Links is a popular destination for golfers from all over the world, and it is also a popular spot for tourists. There are many fine examples of Scottish architecture, and the views over the Firth of Forth are spectacular. The Leith Links also has a long and interesting history, and it is an important part of Scottish culture.

If you’re ready to join the fight and be a planet protector, here are seven tips to get you started.

Wrap Your Pipes in Insulation

One of the biggest threats to our planet is global warming. We often think of the warming of the Earth as something that’s caused by the air outside, but did you know that your plumbing system can contribute to the problem? It’s true – leaky pipes and poorly insulated lines can cause unwanted heat loss. To combat the problem, pipe wrapping insulation is necessary to keep heat in. Without that extra layer of protection, the pipes will lose heat to the surrounding environment, which results in more energy being used to keep the pipes warm enough to function. While the loss of energy itself isn’t much of a threat to the environment, it’s the extra energy needed to keep the pipes warm that causes the issue. Every time your pipes lose heat, your system will automatically turn on to heat them back up again, which causes more emissions to be released into the air. Pipe insulation may seem like a simple change, but by using pipe wrapping insulation, you’ll reduce energy loss, which can help keep the planet cool.

Purchase a Water Heater Timer

Another way to save energy is to purchase a water heater timer. Most water heaters turn on and off throughout the day to keep the water hot, and they tend to stay on for much longer than necessary. Unfortunately, that means more energy is being wasted. Thankfully, there’s a simple solution to the problem: water heater timers. These devices allow you to set the times when you want your water heater to turn on and off. For example, you can choose to have it on from 6 am to 10 am and 6 pm to 10 pm if that’s when you use hot water the most. By choosing your own times, you’re able to reduce the amount of energy being wasted and ensure that your water heater only uses what’s necessary.

Recycle Your Electronics

Most of us are familiar with recycling our paper, plastic, and aluminum products, but what about electronics? It may seem like a simple step, but recycling your old or broken electronics can help protect the planet. Electronics contain many different metals and components that can be harmful to the environment if not recycled properly. By bringing your unwanted electronic items to a recycling center, you’re ensuring that they’ll be disposed of correctly and that the materials will be used to create new products. Some electronics may even be refurbished and resold, which is an added bonus for the environment.

Unplug Your Devices

Many of us fall into the habit of leaving our electronics plugged in, even when they’re not in use. Unfortunately, this can lead to wasted energy and more carbon emissions. When plugged in, devices still draw electricity even when they’re turned off or in standby mode. To combat this issue, try unplugging your devices when they’re not in use. This may seem like a simple step, but it can make a big difference. Not only will you reduce the amount of energy being wasted, but you’ll also save money on your electric bill.

the key factors that impact its effectiveness. The value of warehousing, like any supply chain activity, depends on the timing and spatial execution of the distribution center. The distribution center becomes obsolete only when the central warehouse is unable to offer a competitive advantage to the firm in terms of cost or time. Generally, the advantage is driven by the proximity of the warehouse to the final customer, which allows shorter delivery times and lower inventory carrying costs. For firms that operate in a fragmented market, a central warehouse might not offer such an advantage. The timing of the distribution center in the supply chain is also critical. It takes some time to deliver supplies from the warehouse to the distribution center and then onwards to the final customer. This lead time reduces the responsiveness of the supply chain to changes in customer demand. The distribution center becomes obsolete when the additional costs of carrying higher inventory levels exceed the benefits of shorter delivery times. 2 The distribution center has also been shown to incur an additional inventory cost due to the lack of direct connection between production and customers. However, it is possible to mitigate this disadvantage by using storage practices such as frequent deliveries, or by connecting the distribution center directly to production. The spatial distribution of the distribution center is also critical to its effectiveness. The distribution center needs to be located near the final customer in order to avoid the additional costs of the distribution center. Hence, the distribution center might add value only when it is located at the final delivery point or at one of the nodes along the final delivery path. The distribution center might also add value when it is located near a primary warehouse. The distribution center is similar to a primary warehouse in that it aggregates supplies from several sources. Hence, the location of the distribution center is influenced by the same factors that influence the location of a primary warehouse. The distribution center becomes obsolete when the additional costs of carrying higher inventory levels exceed the benefits of shorter delivery times. The distribution center may also add value when it is near the final delivery point or a node on the final delivery path. The distribution center should also be considered during the design phase of the supply chain. It is also important to understand that the value of the distribution center depends on several factors including the firm's objectives, the products being distributed, the market structure and the geographic conditions. Hence, a generalized decision is not possible for all cases. The distribution center may either add value or become obsolete, depending on the specific case. As a result, it is important to analyze and assess the value of the distribution center on a case-by-case basis.

Unless your blood pressure is high or your doctor tells you otherwise, you may not need to monitor your blood pressure more frequently than this. Some people, however, need to take their blood pressure more frequently, which requires the use of a blood pressure monitor at home. People with high blood pressure, heart disease or diabetes will want to measure their blood pressure more regularly. People who have undergone a recent change in their lifestyle, including losing weight or taking a new medication, will want to measure their blood pressure more frequently. How Often Should You Take Your Blood Pressure If your blood pressure is high or your lifestyle changes, you should check your blood pressure twice a day to monitor it more closely. If you check your blood pressure too frequently, it can cause anxiety, which can raise your blood pressure. How Often Should You Take Your Blood Pressure If you have low blood pressure, checking it too frequently can cause anxiety, which can raise your blood pressure. When Should You Take Your Blood Pressure? Generally, blood pressure is lowest in the morning just after you wake up. It will then rise during the day and peak in the late afternoon. As a result, taking your blood pressure at any time during the day will not give you an accurate picture of your blood pressure, and it should not be used to diagnose high blood pressure. Ideally, you should take your blood pressure sitting down after you have had a few minutes to rest. You should not take your blood pressure right after exercising or right before bed. What Causes High Blood Pressure? The cause of high blood pressure is often unknown and goes by the name “essential hypertension.” In about 5 to 10 percent of cases, it can be traced to a direct cause. This is known as secondary hypertension. For most people, high blood pressure can be traced to factors such as obesity, smoking, excessive alcohol use, stress, lack of exercise and poor diet. The right blood pressure monitor can help you take control of your blood pressure.

cropland extent products capture individual farm fields, small or large, and are crucial for developing accurate higher-level cropland products such as cropping intensities, crop types, crop watering methods (irrigated or rainfed), crop productivity, and crop water productivity. It also brings many challenges that include handling massively large data volumes, computing power, and collecting resource intensive reference training and validation data over complex geographic and political boundaries. Thereby, this study developed a precise and accurate Landsat 30-m derived cropland extent product for two very important, distinct, diverse, and large countries: Australia and China. The study used of eight bands (blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2, TIR1, and NDVI) of Landsat-8 every 16-day Operational Land Imager (OLI) data for the years 2013–2015. The classification was performed by using a pixel-based supervised random forest (RF) machine learning algorithm (MLA) executed on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) cloud computing platform. Each band was time-composited over 4–6 time-periods over a year using median value for various agro-ecological zones (AEZs) of Australia and China. This resulted in a 32–48-layer mega-file data-cube (MFDC) for each of the AEZs. Reference training and validation data were gathered from: (a) field visits, (b) sub-meter to 5-m very high spatial resolution imagery (VHRI) data, and (c) ancillary sources such as from the National agriculture bureaus. Croplands versus non-croplands knowledge base for training the RF algorithm were derived from MFDC using 958 reference-training samples for Australia and 2130 reference-training samples for China. The resulting 30-m cropland extent product was assessed for accuracies using independent validation samples: 900 for Australia and 1972 for China. The 30-m cropland extent product of Australia showed an overall accuracy of 97.6% with a producer’s accuracy of 98.8% (errors of omissions = 1.2%), and user’s accuracy of 79% (errors of commissions = 21%) for the cropland class. For China, overall accuracies were 94% with a producer’s accuracy of 80% (errors of omissions = 20%), and user’s accuracy of 84.2% (errors of commissions = 15.8%) for cropland class. Total cropland areas of Australia were estimated at 35.1 million hectares and 165.2 million hectares for China. These estimates were higher by 8.6% for Australia and 3.9% for China when compared with the traditionally derived national statistics. The cropland extent product further demonstrated the ability to estimate sub-national cropland areas accurately by providing an R2 value of 0.85 when compared with province-wise cropland areas of China. The study provides a paradigm-shift on how cropland maps are produced using multi-date remote sensing. These products can be browsed at www.croplands.org and made available for download at NASA’s Land Processes Distributed Active Archive Center (LP DAAC) https://www.lpdaac.usgs.gov/node/1282. According to Patricia McConnell, a certified applied animal behaviorist and working border collie owner, the history of the border collie breed is “like a genetics 101 experiment” to see what happens if you breed for ability to work instead of adherence to a physical “breed standard.” In today’s working border collie registries, you will find dogs of all shapes, sizes, and coat types. Despite their varied appearance, working border collies are herding prodigies. They can work magic on any type of stock, from sheep and cattle to poultry and pigs, and do it with such style and ability that they have become the stock dog of choice for ranchers across the globe. “The ideal working border collie has the perfect mixture of balance—the ability to find the exact right point in space and put the exact right amount of pressure on the sheep—and power,” says McConnell. “They are benevolent leaders that can take charge without panicking the sheep and are an absolute joy to work.” However, adds McConnell, border collies are not a dog for everyone. “They need a lot of exercise—mental, too, not just physical,” she explains. “They are bred to listen to their handlers from far away while in a hyperfocused state, so they are very sound- and motionsensitive,” she says. And the single-mindedness that allows them to stay focused on their job in the face of all sorts of distractions can also make them prone to obsessive behaviors. “So they may not be the best match for families with children or for busy, boisterous households,” says McConnell. But if you can give them a job—working stock, racing through an agility course, or leaping after a highflying Frisbee—they can be great dogs both on and off the farm.

The Atholl Family The Atholl Family has had a long and significant connection with Dunkeld area and its people. After the Battle of Dunkeld (1689) much of Dunkeld was re-built and successive Dukes gradually acquired many of the properties during the 18th and 19th centuries. Stanley Hill, now a park, was landscaped by the 2nd Duke in 1730. Duchess Anne, widow of the 6th Duke, founded a girls' school in 1854 and the building still be ars her name. The 8th Duke was the first President of the National Trust for Scotland and his wife, Katharine, Scotland's first woman MP, used her Parliamentary salary to renovate some of the Dunkeld houses. The Little Houses in the Cross and Cathedral Street were given to the Trust by Atholl Estates in 1954. These near-derelict properties were restored by the Trust and the Local Authority to provide homes for local people as well as re-create the 17th-century approach to the magnificent setting of the Cathedral of St. Columba. Ownership of the Fountain was publicly transferred to the National Trust for Scotland in 1991 in a ceremony conducted by the 10th Duke of Atholl attended by his Atholl Highlanders. The Duke had a long association with the Trust and was its President at the time of his death in 1996.
